annotations.text:
Round three: where does "what you've explored" live?

You're right that it's browser tabs — the question is which edge. Four shapes, each drawn in the app's current stone-and-sand voice, spec strip at the bottom of each with the honest tradeoff.

My vote: 1, the filmstrip dock — nothing hides, the ticker keeps its stage, and both reading tiles get wider. 2 scales best past ~8 entries. 3 is your top strip, done as quietly as I could. 4 is cheapest and weakest for the demo.

Peira — look & feel, round two.

Top row: three full-page directions — pick one.
Middle: the draw-on motion, and the cliff A/B you were unsure about.
Bottom: two modal treatments, the type/voice system, and the token sheet.

The 8 program colors never change between directions (they are CVD-validated); only the ground, type, and chrome move.

A — Warm editorial (recommended).
Smallest diff from the shipping app: same layout, same components; cool grey turns to warm paper and Newsreader takes the headings and asides.
Tradeoff: the least adventurous of the three.

B — Stone & sand.
Your squircle + sand instinct taken all the way: borders gone, depth from soft warm shadows, serif-italic section labels.
Tradeoff: italic labels scan slower than caps; needs discipline not to feel pillowy.

C — Ink & paper.
The editorial voice as structure: a broadsheet with hairline rules instead of cards. Most distinctive of the three.
Tradeoff: biggest CSS diff, and without card boundaries the three lower zones lean entirely on the hairlines.

The band, kept honest: only as wide as the actual drop (~$1k of earnings), drawn under the data — not the broad wash you were picturing.
Compare against A and veto freely; the pills stand on their own.

The sand sheet replays its entrance every 5s so you can judge the 240ms scale/fade + backdrop blur you asked about. The paper sheet is the no-motion, no-blur alternative with hierarchy carried by type alone. Either works inside any of the three directions.
